content.text:
Agent Braid says only jobs 1 and 2 are a confirmed conflict. It could not confirm that any pair is safe to run together.

| Pair | Agent Braid result | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Job 1 and job 2 | **Conflicting**: serialize or isolate | Both use `config/staging.yaml`, and job 2 writes to it. Job 1's report could see the old or the new timeouts. |
| Job 1 and job 3 | Unknown: serialize unless there is stronger evidence | No shared files. The effect lists I gave were only partly covered, so the analyzer would not call them independent. |
| Job 2 and job 3 | Unknown: serialize unless there is stronger evidence | No shared files, same coverage limit. |

**What this means in practice**
- Jobs 1 and 2 must not run at the same time. Run job 1 first if you want a report of the current timeouts. Run it after job 2 if you want a report of the new values.
- Job 3 touches only `config/production.yaml`, so it looks safe to run alongside either of the others. Agent Braid did not give that a formal "independent" rating, though. The effect lists came from my description of the jobs. The analyzer did not observe them, and it treats them as partial coverage. It also only compares paths as exact strings. It does not follow symlinks, generated files, or a shared parser or include between the two configs.
- If you want job 3 confirmed as independent, I would need to check the real files, for example whether `staging.yaml` and `production.yaml` share includes or anchors. I have not looked at them.

This was analysis only. Nothing was executed, and the workspace has no execution authority or grant. The evidence is saved at `agent-braid-plugin://3cf77b4c3de6f63ca4c1bf01f3a35191/runs/3749bdb98f214323ba4b54799864089b/evidence/ev-f665a9c4f40e4ba088f1d79055daa511`.
